title: Line-restarting glyph chain with the line end as a symbol, plus copying of nearby words
method: Fitted on the paragraph lines of the public practice training pages only (lines without uncertain readings). Each line is one string of symbols: its glyphs, a word-space symbol between words, a line-end symbol after the last word. The fitted table is how often each symbol follows the four symbols before it, with shorter contexts as fallback. The writer starts fresh at each line and draws symbol by symbol until the line-end symbol comes up, so line length is whatever the chain gives and a word space and a line end are two outcomes of the same draw. At the start of a word, one time in ten, the writer instead copies one of the last ten words written and alters one glyph, the new glyph drawn from the same table in its context; whether a space or a line end follows the copy is again drawn from the table. No word list, no position class, no rule that names a glyph, a position, or any fact. A line holding a four-word run of the manuscript is redrawn. Seed 408, 3,000 lines. Practice split, whole lines kept: 7 of 7 (F-001 14.4 against 61.6; F-002 0.235; F-003 15.7 against 54.6; F-004 0.331; F-005 0.241; F-006 4.81; F-007 0.190 against 0.210). Honest margins: a second seed (7) at the same settings gives 6 of 7, F-003 falling to 9.3 against its threshold of 10; without the copying step the chain alone gives 6 of 7 with wider margins on F-001 (28) and F-003 (20) but misses F-007 (0.131); copying more (one in four) lifts F-007 and loses F-003, because copied line-opening words land mid-line. The copy rate (0.1) and the seed were chosen on the practice split. Because each line restarts the chain, first glyphs of a line do not depend on the last glyph of the line before, which is the collapse of edge dependence at line breaks.
